findings: A positive interaction can mean Muon is less harmful at its own source state; it does not imply benefit at either source state.
The current renderer calls positive averaged state/operator effects additive even when the interaction is significantly negative.
A supported state effect alongside an inconclusive larger operator estimate does not establish state-effect dominance or equivalence of the other effect to zero.
The abstract says it separates the gain although its inputs only contain post-continuation endpoint contrasts, not a decomposition of the primary 500k outcome.
Calibration matches a fixed gradient-history probe direction ratio, not the first realized shuffled-batch update; the frozen protocol explicitly clarifies this distinction.
